## New variable creation based on existing variable

### To create new variable from existing when you are given initial population population (base of 2022 population size) growth rate(differ to each & every country),natural logarithm (2.71828) and time period(8 years.

```{r Pop in 2030}
time<- 2030-2022
world_pop$Pop_2030 <- world_pop$`2022 Population` *exp((world_pop$`Growth Rate` - 1) * 8)
```

## Extracting top ten countries with largest number of population

```{r top ten countries}
top_ten<-world_pop[order(world_pop$`2020 Population`,decreasing = TRUE),][1:10,]
top_ten

```
### By using ggplo2# graph showing the visualization of countries vs population 


```{r graph of top ten}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
ggplot(top10, aes(x = reorder(`Country/Territory`, `2022 Population`),
                  y = `2022 Population`)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Countries by Population (2022)",
       x = "Country",
       y = "Population")
```
## Trend in population since 1990-2022 
### The graph ggplot2 used to show the the trend of population since 1990 to 2022

```{r trend in population}
trend <- pivot_longer(top10,
                      cols = c(`1990 Population`, `2000 Population`,
                               `2010 Population`, `2015 Population`,
                               `2020 Population`, `2022 Population`),
                      names_to = "Year",
                      values_to = "Population")

trend$Year <- as.numeric(substr(trend$Year, 1, 4))

ggplot(trend, aes(x = Year, y = Population, color = `Country/Territory`)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1990, 2000, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2022)) +
  labs(title = "Population Trend, 1990 to 2022 (Top 10 Countries)",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Population",
       color = "Country")
trend
```
